description: Figure 2, titled “Original distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset. Percentages are displayed with respect to number of utterances,” is a pie chart that visually represents the proportional breakdown of five emotion categories present in the IEMOCAP dataset. The chart is divided into five distinct slices, each corresponding to one of the following emotions: neutral, frustration, sadness, anger, and happiness. Although the specific percentage values and color assignments for each slice are not legible in the provided image, the relative sizes of the slices suggest that “neutral” constitutes the largest portion of the dataset, followed by “frustration” and “sadness,” while “anger” and “happiness” appear to represent smaller, more comparable proportions. The chart includes a legend (implied by the caption and standard practice) to associate each color with its corresponding emotion label, and the percentages are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice to indicate their share of the total number of utterances. The overall layout is clean and typical for categorical distribution visualization, with no exploded slices or additional annotations visible.
